confidence: Moderate confidence in targeted glass contamination, low confidence in identity. Shared punch and food results narrow method; the 6:32–6:44 opportunity remains conditional on the service manager's custody account.
plausibility_notes: Actual service differs from advance program: unwrapped 6:32 rather than planned 6:40. This is a useful fair correction because the earlier document explicitly said planned, not attendance.
An unpaid extra-course dispute drawing a server back to the kitchen is a plausible operational distraction, and collection on a tray is ordinary service behavior.

The precise four-stage photographs are convenient. A service manager could document an unusual donor setup, but why photograph a still-wrapped shop glass and later collection and pour should be motivated.
No image pixels are provided here, only captions and a photo identifier, so I cannot independently assess what the photographs actually prove.

The first report mentioned cover sealing at 6:44; current actual account describes collection, with no cover. This is not a contradiction if plans changed, but players should not carry the planned sealed cover into the actual timeline.
Server custody does not by itself clear all catering staff or prove poison was present before 6:44; it becomes a firm bracket only if the account and handling are independently supported.
Cyanide in only Grant's glass strongly favors deliberate individual targeting. It does not yet establish that the empty bottle supplied that cyanide.
Late admission excludes the preparation walkthrough only if independently verified and exhaustive; it does not exclude access to the exposed glass or poison obtained elsewhere.
